title: Docstring/spec claim the committed script re-renders byte-identical to the committed PNGs — false after the geometry rework
evidence:
+Pipeline VALIDATED on Blender 5.2.0 LTS: the render is pixel-deterministic
+(decoded pixels byte-identical to the committed sheet; only PNG-encoder
+metadata differs), so a no-op re-render is golden-safe — only committed
+geometry changes trigger the T2 re-bless (docs/silhouette-spec.md §3).
+- **Deterministic render proven**: re-running the OLD script on Blender
+- **PNGs intentionally unchanged in this PR** (`git checkout` after the
+HOST_SIZE      = (0.85, 1.10)   # flat tower block — PORTRAIT aspect ~0.77, 1.75 tiles
detail: Determinism was proven with the OLD script; PNGs are intentionally unchanged. The committed script's geometry (host portrait 0.85×1.10 vs old 1.14×0.88) cannot render byte-identical to the committed sheet — 'no-op re-render is golden-safe' is now false.
recommended_fix: Reword the docstring and spec §3: determinism proven for the pre-rework script; running the committed script changes sprite bytes and requires the T2 re-bless.

title: PR-body bbox 'measured' aspects are geometrically impossible (uniformly scaled pucks must share one aspect)
evidence:
+  | puck_1/2/3 | 158/180/202 wide | 1.09–1.19 | discs, tier ladder |
+PUCK_TIER      = {4: 1.0, 8: 1.15, 16: 1.30}   # tier size ladder (keep)
+    r = PUCK_R * PUCK_TIER[ports]
+    shot(sc, name, 0.95)
detail: The three pucks are one disc uniformly scaled under one fixed camera and pad — bbox aspect must be identical across tiers (widths 158/180/202 do match the scale ratios); a 1.09–1.19 spread cannot be measured output. Flat-rect rows imply incompatible foreshortening (0.75–0.89).
recommended_fix: Re-measure the real bboxes or drop the unverifiable table; do not ship reconstructed numbers as render evidence ('New geometry verified').

title: Outline ring width stated three incompatible ways: README +~0.03, spec §0 +~0.06, code +0.03 per side
evidence:
+| Outline | thin dark ink `#33414F` plate at the base, footprint + ~0.03 (≈2px in-game ring) |
+| Outline | thin dark ink plate `#33414F` at base, footprint + ~0.06 (≈2px in-game ring) | MM's defining edge |
+OUTLINE_RING = 0.03   # ink ring width around the fill (scene units, ~2px in-game)
+    add_cube(name + "_o", (cx, cy, OUTLINE_H / 2), (fw + 2 * OUTLINE_RING, fd + 2 * OUTLINE_RING, OUTLINE_H),
detail: README says footprint +~0.03; spec §0 says +~0.06; the code adds OUTLINE_RING per side (+0.06 total). Both docs claim '≈2px in-game' from different numbers — the user sculpts against this 'must match' contract.
recommended_fix: Align all three on one definition, e.g. 'outline plate = footprint + 0.06 total (OUTLINE_RING 0.03 per side)'.

title: Spec says the house ridge runs along the long axis; the code puts it along Y — the short axis
evidence:
+- **Geometry:** flat gable rect — rect footprint, ridge along the long axis, the
     """Gable roof with the ridge along Y and a per-face tone split (the +X
+HOUSE_SIZE     = (0.62, 0.56)   # gable rect — near-square, in-game 1.50 tiles
+    add_gable(name + "_roof", bw, bd, GABLE_RIDGE, OUTLINE_H, hex_color)
detail: Footprint is 0.62 (X) × 0.56 (Y): the long axis is X, but add_gable's ridge runs along Y. The spec instructs the live-in-Blender user to build the opposite orientation from the default render.
recommended_fix: Pick one orientation: fix the spec wording, or swap HOUSE_SIZE / the gable call so the ridge actually runs along the long axis.
